title: Tenali Raman Tale 133

full_text:
An eccentric visiting mathematician from Ujjain, Master Aryabhatta II, challenged the scholars of Vijayanagara with a culinary puzzle:
'I place five dried black peppercorns upon this table.
I challenge any mathematician in this court to divide these five peppercorns equally among three scholars, so that each scholar receives an identical whole number of peppercorns, without cutting, grinding, crushing, or breaking a single peppercorn, and without leaving any peppercorns on the table!'

The court mathematicians argued for two hours:
'Five cannot be divided by three without fractions! Five divided by three is one and two-thirds! It is mathematically impossible without cutting the peppercorns!'

Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, the division is simple and mathematically flawless!'

Tenali called the three scholars forward to the table: Scholar A, Scholar B, and Scholar C.
Tenali picked up the five peppercorns.
He handed **one peppercorn** to Scholar A.
He handed **one peppercorn** to Scholar B.
He handed **one peppercorn** to Scholar C.

Tenali then picked up the remaining two peppercorns, looked at Scholar A, Scholar B, and Scholar C, and said:
'Now, brothers, look at the table:
Has each of you received an identical whole number of peppercorns?'
The three scholars answered: 'Yes! Each of us has received exactly one whole peppercorn!'
Tenali asked: 'Was any peppercorn cut, crushed, or broken?'
'No, all are whole!'
Tenali asked: 'And are there any peppercorns left on the table?'
'No, the table is clean!'

Tenali then popped the remaining two peppercorns straight into his own mouth, chewed them with a loud crunch, and swallowed them with a smile!
'And these two peppercorns are the mathematician’s consulting fee paid to Tenali Raman for resolving the dispute!'

The entire court erupted in roaring laughter!
The visiting mathematician stared in utter bewilderment, then broke into appreciative applause:
'Brilliant! The puzzle stated that each scholar must receive an identical whole number without breaking any, and that none remain on the table!
Tenali fulfilled every single condition with practical wit!'
King Krishnadevaraya rewarded Tenali with a purse of silver, celebrating that practical wisdom outshines theoretical rigidities.
moral: Simplicity and sharp wit solve riddles where complex mathematics creates confusion.
